key_insight: A weakly supervised NLP and claims-based approach can identify anaphylaxis from EHR data with strong discrimination, especially when text-derived silver labels are used.
clinical_relevance: This could support scalable, multi-site phenotyping for anaphylaxis research and surveillance without relying on heavily manual chart review.
method: Collected potential anaphylaxis events from Kaiser Permanente Washington and Vanderbilt University Medical Center.
Engineered features from clinical text using automated NLP and combined them with diagnosis-code information.
Trained phenotyping models using four silver labels and compared them against gold-standard abstracted outcomes.
evidence_signal: The best reported model reached an AUC of 0.931 at KPWA, with PPV 0.52–0.77 and sensitivity 0.78–1.00 depending on site and model.
watch_item: Performance varied by health system, so local documentation practices and text availability may limit portability without site-specific validation.
paper_title: Identifying anaphylaxis using weakly-supervised prediction models and natural language processing
